title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Return true when the tree is a valid BST. The left subtree of every node contains only smaller keys, and the right subtree contains only larger keys. Comparing a node with its parent is not enough.
constraints: Node values fit in a 32-bit signed integer
hints: An inorder traversal of a BST is strictly increasing.
Alternatively, carry an exclusive lower and upper bound into each subtree.
The bounds start as negative and positive infinity. A left child tightens the upper bound. A right child tightens the lower bound.

approaches.name: Inorder list
approaches.explanation: Check that the sequence is strictly sorted.

approaches.name: Bound propagation
approaches.explanation: Every node is checked against the range inherited from its ancestors.

editorial: The bug in 'greater than parent' is a node deep in the left subtree that is still larger than the root. Bounds fix that: every ancestor contributes a constraint. Inorder works for the same reason: the BST definition is exactly that inorder is sorted.

examples.explanation: 3 is in the right subtree of 5 but is smaller than 5.
